source.name: Hidden Profile diagnostic set
source.note: Small authored smoke-test set for genuine two-agent informational dependence. Not a wholesale HiddenBench import: HiddenBench uses N-agent flat hidden lists without pre-assigned A/B visibility or evidence-structure tags. These items use explicit shared / a_private / b_private units and evaluator-only metadata.

items.title: Engineering hire: Avery, Blake, or Casey
items.question: Which candidate should the team hire for the staff engineer role?

information.text: The role requires both strong systems design skill and reliable delivery under deadline pressure.
All three candidates passed the initial screen and are available to start within a month.
Hiring committee policy: prefer the candidate who is acceptable on both technical depth and delivery reliability, not the extreme on only one axis.
Technical interview scores (out of 100): Avery 94, Blake 71, Casey 86.
Avery led a complex distributed-systems redesign that reviewers rated as unusually strong.
Blake's take-home showed several gaps in concurrency and failure-mode reasoning.
Reference calls: Avery had three late critical deliveries and a peer conflict on the last team; Blake had zero late deliveries in two years; Casey had one minor slip that was resolved cleanly.
Blake's manager describes Blake as the most dependable engineer on a high-pressure on-call rotation.
Casey is rated solid-reliable by two independent references, with no red flags.

evaluatorMetadata.notes: A alone overweights Avery (tech). B alone overweights Blake (reliability). Combined, Casey is the only candidate acceptable on both axes under S3.

items.title: Evacuation route under incomplete reports
items.question: Which evacuation destination is actually reachable right now?

information.text: All three destinations normally take about the same time by car from the village.
West City hotels are ready; East Town has volunteer support; North Hill school can shelter people for two weeks.
Only one destination is currently reachable. Choosing a blocked route strands the group.
Radio from the tunnel crew: the East Town tunnel is blocked by a stalled supply truck and cannot be cleared today.
River gauge at the West bridge still reads below flood stage; the West bridge structure looks intact from the south bank.
Fire service update: a brush fire has closed the West City approach road beyond the bridge; traffic cannot pass.
North Hill walking trails were closed earlier for fallen trees, but the paved driveway was confirmed clear one hour ago and remains open.

evaluatorMetadata.notes: A's private packet makes West look open and East blocked. B's private packet makes West blocked and North open. Combined: East and West blocked → North Hill.

items.title: Classic hidden profile: Candidate Ren vs Candidate Sol
items.question: Which candidate is better supported once all evidence is considered?

information.text: Ren has strong public speaking skills and a polished interview presence.
Ren's resume lists several well-known employers.
Sol's interview was quieter and less flashy than Ren's.
Both candidates meet the minimum qualifications.
Ren's last two managers report missed roadmap commitments on multi-quarter projects.
Sol quietly delivered a cross-team reliability program that cut incident volume by 40%.
Independent audit notes: Ren's claimed impact numbers on the resume are substantially inflated.
Sol's references describe unusually careful decision-making under incomplete information.

evaluatorMetadata.notes: Shared cues make Ren look attractive. Private cues, when pooled, favor Sol and undermine Ren.

items.title: Plant fault: sensor drift vs coolant leak
items.question: What is the most strongly supported cause of the plant alarm?

information.text: Alarm A-17 fired twice in the last hour on Loop 3. Production is paused pending diagnosis.
Operator error is possible in principle but the checklist for this shift was signed and camera review shows no bypass of lockout steps.
A senior technician verbally recalls that Loop 3 sensors have drifted before and says Sensor drift is the usual cause of A-17.
The senior technician did not bring calibration logs; the recollection is from memory of prior incidents.
Fresh lab assay from Loop 3 coolant shows contaminant levels consistent with an active leak, not with sensor-only faults.
Independent pressure-decay test on Loop 3 failed twice; the instrumentation shop already re-zeroed the primary sensor and the alarm still recurs.

evaluatorMetadata.notes: A holds weaker authority-flavored evidence for Sensor drift. B holds stronger objective tests for Coolant leak. Evaluator strength labels are not shown to agents.
